step2.title: Enter EDL Mode

step3.title: Connect Device
step3.description: Select your device model from the dropdown and click 'Connect Device'. Wait for the connection process to complete.

step4.title: Load ROM or Select Partitions

q1.question: Is Q-Flash safe to use?
q1.answer: Yes, Q-Flash uses official Qualcomm EDL protocols, the same as manufacturer tools. However, always backup important data before flashing.

q2.question: Will flashing void my warranty?
q2.answer: It depends on manufacturer policy. Generally, unlocking bootloader or flashing custom firmware may void warranty. Check with your device manufacturer.

q3.question: Can I unbrick my device with Q-Flash?
q3.answer: Yes, if your device can enter EDL mode and you have the correct stock ROM, Q-Flash can restore your device.

q4.question: What's the difference between backup and flash?
q4.answer: Backup saves partition data from device to PC. Flash writes partition data from PC to device. Always backup before flashing.

q5.question: Can I use this on Mac or Linux?
q5.answer: Currently Q-Flash Web Tool requires Windows due to WinUSB driver requirements. Mac/Linux support may be added in future.

q6.question: Why does my device need VIP authentication?
q6.answer: Oppo, OnePlus, and Realme devices require VIP authentication for security. This is a manufacturer requirement, not a Q-Flash limitation.

q7.question: How long does flashing take?
q7.answer: Depends on partition sizes and USB speed. Typically 5-15 minutes for full ROM flash. Individual partitions may take seconds to minutes.

q8.question: Can I flash custom ROMs?
q8.answer: Yes, as long as the ROM is compatible with your device chipset and you have the correct partition images and rawprogram files.

q1.question: What is EDL mode and why do I need it?
q1.answer: EDL (Emergency Download) mode is a special boot mode on Qualcomm devices that allows low-level access for flashing firmware. It's required because it bypasses normal Android restrictions and enables direct partition access.

q2.question: Is Q-Flash safe for my device?
q2.answer: Yes, Q-Flash uses official Qualcomm EDL protocols - the same protocols used by manufacturer tools. However, always backup critical partitions before flashing, and ensure you're using the correct ROM for your device model.

q3.question: Can Q-Flash unbrick my device?
q3.answer: In most cases, yes. If your device can enter EDL mode (test point method works even for hard-bricked devices), Q-Flash can restore it by flashing stock firmware. Make sure you have the correct stock ROM for your specific device variant.

q4.question: Why does my device need VIP authentication?
q4.answer: Oppo, OnePlus, and Realme devices require VIP (Verified Image Programming) authentication as a security measure. This ensures only authorized firmware can be flashed. Q-Flash handles this automatically with proper firehose files.

q5.question: Which browsers are supported?
q5.answer: Q-Flash requires a Chromium-based browser (Chrome, Edge, Brave) version 89 or later with WebUSB support. Firefox and Safari are not supported due to lack of WebUSB API.

q6.question: How long does flashing take?
q6.answer: Time depends on partition sizes and USB speed. Individual partitions can take seconds to minutes. A full ROM flash typically takes 5-15 minutes. Large partitions like 'super' may take longer.

troubleshoot.title: Cannot connect to device
troubleshoot.description: Failed to connect to the device. Possible causes:
troubleshoot.reason1_desc: The EDL mode on your phone may have timed out. Please try entering EDL mode again!
troubleshoot.reason2_desc: Use Device Manager on Windows to check and change the driver to WinUSB (QUSB_BULK).
troubleshoot.reason3_desc: If the device shows "Qualcomm HS-USB QDLoader 9008" in Device Manager, manually switch the driver to WinUSB or use Zadig.
troubleshoot.help_text: See detailed guide on the Q-Flash Support page
